'''Taylor Lockwood Booth''' (September 22, 1933 &ndash; October 20, 1986) was a [[mathematician]] known for his work in [[automata theory]].

One of his fundamental works is ''Sequential Machines and Automata Theory'' (1967). It is a wide-ranging book meant for specialists, written for both theoretical computer scientists as well as electrical engineers. It deals with [[Minimal realization|state minimization]] techniques, [[finite-state machine]]s, [[Turing machine]]s, [[Markov process]]es, and [[undecidable problem|undecidability]].

==Education==
Booth studied at the [[University of Connecticut]], where he received his B.S., M.S. and Ph.D. degrees.<ref name="Tribute">{{cite web |url=http://www.computer.org/portal/web/awards/taylortribute |title=Tribute to Taylor L. Booth |publisher=[[IEEE Computer Society|IEEE-CS]] |accessdate={{Format date|2010|10|23}} |archive-date=2010-06-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100617040310/http://www.computer.org/portal/web/awards/taylortribute |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
At his alma mater Booth was professor at the [[Computer Science]] and [[Computer Engineering|Engineering]] department.<ref name="Tribute" />

He was the founder and director of the Computer Applications & Research Center (CARC) at the [[University of Connecticut]]'s School of Engineering. In 1981 the center was created to support the school's growing need for centralized computing research and development services. After his death the center was renamed to "Taylor L. Booth Center for Computer Applications and Research" or in its shorter form the "Booth Research Center". In 2002 this merged with the Advanced Technology Institute (ATI), another center at the School of Engineering, to form the "Booth Engineering Center for Advanced Technology" (BECAT).<ref name="Tribute" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.becat.uconn.edu/bctoverview.htm |title=BECAT Overview and History |publisher=[[University of Connecticut]] |accessdate={{Format date|2010|10|28}} |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100622180250/http://www.becat.uconn.edu/bctoverview.htm |archivedate=2010-06-22 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.engr.uconn.edu/pdf/annual2002.pdf |title=School of Engineering Annual report 2001-2002 |publisher=[[University of Connecticut]] |accessdate={{Format date|2020|09|17}} |archive-date=2016-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303182603/http://www.engr.uconn.edu/pdf/annual2002.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Booth was the first president of the Computing Sciences Accreditation Board, founded in 1984 and since renamed to [[CSAB (professional organization)|CSAB]].<ref name="Tribute" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.computer.org/portal/web/pressroom/2007/top60 |title=IEEE Computer Society Marks 60th Anniversary |publisher=[[IEEE Computer Society|IEEE-CS]] |date={{Format date|2007|8|7}} |accessdate={{Format date|2010|10|23}} |archive-date=2011-06-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629144630/http://www.computer.org/portal/web/pressroom/2007/top60 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Professor Booth received following awards and honors:<ref name="Tribute" />
* The [[Frederick Emmons Terman Award]] from the [[American Society for Engineering Education]] in 1972, to recognize the outstanding young electrical engineering educator.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.asee.org/member-resources/awards/full-list-of-awards/awards-archive/past-division-award-winners-2#Electrical_and_Computer_Engineering_Division |title=Past Frederick Emmons Terman Award Winners |publisher=[[American Society for Engineering Education]] |accessdate={{Format date|2010|11|3}} |archive-date=2013-04-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130402171545/http://www.asee.org/member-resources/awards/full-list-of-awards/awards-archive/past-division-award-winners-2#Electrical_and_Computer_Engineering_Division |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* The [[IEEE Centennial Medal]] from the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) in 1984.
* The Distinguished Service Award from the [[IEEE Computer Society]] in 1985, for his accreditation work.

===Taylor L. Booth Education Award===
After Booth's death, the IEEE Computer Society established the Taylor L. Booth Education Award, to keep his name in memory. The award is given annually for individuals with an "outstanding record in computer science and engineering education".<ref name="Tribute" /><ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.computer.org/volunteering/awards/booth
|title=Taylor L. Booth Education Award
|date=3 April 2018
|publisher=[[IEEE Computer Society|IEEE-CS]]
|accessdate={{Format date|2022|07|09}}}}</ref>
